full.description: This image is a photomicrograph of a skin biopsy stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The section shows features of interface dermatitis with epidermal changes such as keratinocyte apoptosis, basal layer vacuolization, and mild perivascular lymphocytic infiltration in the dermis. These histologic findings are characteristic of cutaneous lupus erythematosus or a related interface dermatitis process.

blind.description: This is a micrograph of a skin biopsy showing the dermis. The tissue exhibits noncaseating epithelioid granulomas containing Langhans' giant cells, characterized by a paucity of lymphocytes. These findings are consistent with naked granulomas in the dermis, which are often indicative of granulomatous dermatoses such as sarcoidosis.

random.description: This is a micrograph showing a skin biopsy sample stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The section displays epidermal changes alongside a superficial and perivascular lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrate in the dermis. Findings are consistent with an inflammatory dermatosis, potentially suggestive of lupus erythematosus or a similar interface dermatitis pattern. Further clinical correlation would be required for a definitive diagnosis.
